CODERED ’26 / STUDENT CHALLENGE BRIEF
  Agnes AI Track
  AI for Science and Physical AI



  WHAT YOU ARE BUILDING

   Build a functional product that helps a defined user complete a scientific, engineering or
   physical-world task and demonstrate its usefulness with evidence.


  How to use this brief

  Choose one focused problem within this track. You are free to select the implementation, supporting tools and interface. A
  narrow workflow with a reproducible result is sufficient. The product directions below are starting points, not fixed problem
  statements. You may also propose another relevant scientific, engineering or physical-world problem with a clear user and
  evaluation method.

  1. Track Overview

  Build a working product that uses Agnes AI to help a defined user solve a scientific, engineering or physical-world problem.
  Choose a focused task, connect AI outputs to tools, data or simulation, and show measurable value against a baseline.

   Track                                AI for Science and Physical AI, including scientific research, engineering optimization and
                                        disaster-response support.


   Challenge type                       Product Innovation / New Product Development. Enhancements to an existing product are welcome when
                                        the team identifies its new contribution.

   Technology                           Agnes AI offers public text, image and video APIs that teams can use within scientific and engineering
                                        workflows.

  2. Context and Problem to Solve

  Scientific and engineering work often involves moving between documents, data, code and specialist tools. This track asks
  teams to connect an AI capability to a concrete user task and validate the output through domain tools, data or simulation. The
  aim is a useful prototype that can support a later discussion with researchers or potential users.

   How can AI help a researcher, engineer or response planner complete a specific task more
   effectively, while making its outputs possible to check? Choose one user, one workflow
   bottleneck and one measurable outcome.


  Consider the following when defining your problem:
   Problem and users: Researchers, engineers and planners can spend substantial time translating requirements into
  experiments, code, analyses or plans. Choose a concrete bottleneck rather than treating an entire scientific field as the
  problem.

   Workflow stage: Focus on a defined stage of a real or realistic workflow, such as validating a small design, tuning a compute
  kernel, reviewing protein research or planning a simulated rescue response.

   Current limitations: Manual handoffs and isolated AI responses can leave users with outputs they still need to verify or
  translate into a usable result. Identify the specific limitation in your baseline.

   Evidence: Substantiate the problem with cited domain material, a representative task or user feedback. Compare your
  prototype and baseline using the same inputs and evaluation conditions.







CODERED ’26  /  AGNES AI TRACK                                                                                                                         01

3. Suggested Product Directions

  Choose one direction and narrow it to a specific user, task and measurable outcome. The examples below describe possible
  starting points; teams define their own solution.

   01 Chip Design & Verification

   Help users turn a small set of design requirements into a candidate implementation or testbench, then check it with permitted
   simulation or verification tools. A suitable outcome is fewer invalid designs or less time to reach a passing test case.

   02 Operator Optimization

   Help developers improve a selected numerical or AI operator. Measure runtime against an initial implementation on the same
   hardware and inputs, while preserving numerical correctness.

   03 Protein Synthesis Research Support

   Help researchers organize published evidence or permitted sequence data around a narrowly defined protein research question.
   Provide traceable sources and checks for accuracy. Wet-lab synthesis and biological validation are outside the required
   prototype.

   04 Disaster Response & Rescue Planning

   Help planners turn public or synthetic incident information into a reviewed situation summary, resource plan or simulated search
   route. Evaluate under stated scenario constraints and retain human review.

  4. Users and Product Opportunity


   Potential users                         Researchers, engineering teams, scientific developers and disaster-response planners. Select a specific
                                           user and workflow.

   Other stakeholders                      Domain experts, research supervisors, infrastructure operators and organizations that could test or adopt
                                           the product.

   Current workflow                        The user gathers data and requirements, chooses a method, runs tools or simulations, checks results and
                                           decides what to do next. Identify the step your product will improve.

   Common pain points                      Repeated manual work, fragmented tools, hard-to-check AI outputs and limited time or computing
                                           resources for testing alternatives.


   User outcome                            Help the chosen user move from a task or question to a checked output that can be used in the next step
                                           of their workflow.

   Meaningful improvement                  Show improvement in correctness, speed, effort, cost or planning quality relative to a stated baseline.
                                           Choose the metric that fits your task.

   Distinct value                          Combine AI capability with a usable workflow and credible validation. Explain the contribution beyond an
                                           isolated model response or existing tool.

























CODERED ’26  /  AGNES AI TRACK                                                                                                                                    02

5. Expected Product Capabilities


   Must-have                                 A working user workflow; meaningful use of at least one Agnes AI model in the product; traceable inputs
                                             and outputs; and a repeatable way to evaluate the result. Coding assistance alone does not demonstrate
                                             Agnes-powered product functionality.

   Nice-to-have                              Integration with domain tools or simulation, source citations, experiment history, uncertainty reporting or
                                             improvement across repeated attempts. Additional modalities are optional.

   User interaction                          A user supplies a task, data or scenario, reviews the proposed output and supporting evidence, and can
                                             revise, approve or reject the result. Teams choose their own interface and architecture.

   What to demonstrate                       A GitHub repository accessible for review, a README showing where Agnes is used and which models
                                             power each feature, and a short working demo. Include setup instructions, a reproducible test case,
                                             baseline results, limitations and known failure cases.

   6. Technical and Operational Constraints


   API limits and reliability                Free/default-account requests per minute (RPM) are dynamic and depend on model, resolution and
                                             platform capacity; use the current console limits [1]. Credits do not remove rate limits or guarantee
                                             capacity. Handle HTTP 429 and temporary service failures. Video generation can return HTTP 503 or a
                                             queue-full response during capacity pressure; allow bounded retries with backoff and a clear failure state
                                             [2].

   Performance and accuracy                  Define task-specific targets and compare against a stated baseline using a documented test set. Report
                                             correctness or quality alongside time, API usage and cost where relevant. Video is optional; prepare a
                                             clearly labelled recording of an actual run if live generation is delayed.

   Security and data                         Keep API keys server-side or in protected local configuration; exclude secrets from repositories and
                                             demos. Use public, synthetic or explicitly permitted data. Identify dataset licenses and obtain permission
                                             before using personal or confidential material.


   Hardware and deployment                   API calls require internet access. Teams provide their own computing environment and domain-specific
                                             tools. No dedicated GPU, robot, laboratory, chip fabrication facility or private research API is included.
                                             Simulation and small-scale tests are acceptable.


   Safety                                    Use simulation, public data and expert review appropriate to the task. Scientific outputs require
                                             independent validation. Disaster-response and robotics demonstrations must remain supervised
                                             prototypes, with human approval before consequential actions. Wet-lab work, real emergency dispatch
                                             and autonomous operation in hazardous settings are not required.

   7. Agnes AI Resources

   Current published free offers cover Agnes 2.5 Flash and 3.0 Flash text models, Flash image models and Video 2.5 Flash.
   Check pricing and account permissions before use [3]; rate limits and capacity still apply.

   Rounds 1 and 2                            Use the existing free API offering under its current availability and limits.

   Finalist API balance                      The 12 finalist teams receive US$10 per registered member, credited individually. A three-member team
                                             therefore has US$30 in aggregate balances; a four-member team has US$40. Each balance remains on
                                             its own account.

   Account setup                             Each finalist member must create an account at platform.agnes-ai.com and provide their registered email
                                             for credit allocation. Passwords and API keys are not required by the organiser.


   Credits                                   Sponsored balances do not expire and remain available after the event until used. Credit activation timing
                                             is coordinated by the organiser. Further funding is not committed.

   Data                                      Teams may use public, synthetic or properly licensed datasets that fit their chosen problem. Agnes AI has
                                             not committed a proprietary scientific dataset; document data provenance and permitted use.










CODERED ’26  /  AGNES AI TRACK                                                                                                                                              03

Development environment                   Teams may build local test environments or simulations. A dedicated event sandbox, reserved inference
                                             capacity and specialist hardware are not currently committed.

   Documentation and tools                   Public API documentation, model guides, pricing and error-handling references [1–3]. Agnes Harness is
                                             available as an optional public development resource [4]; using it does not imply access to private
                                             research systems.

   8. How to Evaluate Your Product

   Demonstrate success on a bounded task with a stated baseline, reproducible inputs and relevant measurements. The final
   judging rules are to be confirmed by the organiser.

   Functional result                         Demonstrate an end-to-end workflow on a reproducible case, including actual Agnes model use and
                                             handling of invalid inputs or API failure.

   User value                                Explain who benefits and compare effort, usability or decision quality with the current workflow. Include
                                             user or expert feedback where available; identify assumptions where it is unavailable.

   Technical evidence                        Report a relevant baseline and metric, such as test pass rate for generated code, operator runtime at
                                             equal numerical correctness, source accuracy for research assistance, or planning results under a
                                             simulated scenario. Include limitations and failures, not only the best run.

   Cost and feasibility                      Report approximate cost and time per completed task and explain what would be needed for a small pilot.

   Responsible design                        Show data provenance, protected credentials, clear uncertainty and appropriate human review.
                                             Distinguish generated suggestions from validated results. Report retries and failures for workflows that
                                             depend on external APIs.

   9. Scope and Boundaries


   In scope                                  A focused scientific, engineering or physical-world workflow with meaningful Agnes model use, a working
                                             prototype and measurable evaluation. Third-party tools, open-source software and simulations may be
                                             used as permitted by their licenses and event rules.


   Out of scope                              A generic chat wrapper without a defined domain task; a concept deck without working functionality;
                                             unsupported claims of scientific discovery, production readiness or autonomous rescue. Full-scale
                                             fabrication, wet-lab validation and training a foundation model are not required.

   Acceptable simplifications                Small datasets, toy circuits, CPU-scale benchmarks, synthetic incidents and simulated environments are
                                             acceptable. State assumptions, label prerecorded demonstrations, and disclose how a simplified test
                                             differs from real deployment.

   Dependencies                              Registered API accounts for finalist credit allocation; internet access; permitted datasets and external
                                             tools; and the organiser's submission rules.

   10. Business and Adoption Context

   Explain who could use your product after the event and what evidence would justify a small follow-up test.


   Alternatives                              Compare with the chosen manual workflow, existing domain software or a simple AI baseline. Name an
                                             appropriate alternative and compare the same task under similar conditions.

   Potential value                           Reduced task time or repetitive work, better engineering performance at equal correctness, improved
                                             evidence checking, or more useful planning outputs. Quantify the benefit your prototype actually
                                             demonstrates.

   Adoption pathway                          Validate the prototype with a relevant user or expert, document remaining gaps, and identify a small
                                             follow-up test. Further discussion with Agnes AI researchers or partners is possible by mutual interest and
                                             is not guaranteed.

   [2] API integration and error handling
